reviewer: solo new-family build 2026-07-21: ESM-2 protein masked-LM proven FIRST in headless Chrome (AutoModelForMaskedLM + AutoTokenizer, WASM q8). At hemoglobin β6 the model reconstructs the wild-type Glu (E, rank 0) and scores the sickle-cell E6V substitution at LLR −2.3 (strongly deleterious), more damaging than the conservative E6D (−1.25) — the published zero-shot variant-effect behaviour. The deployed page was then driven end-to-end (validate-protein-mutation-oracle.mjs). No media — all input is a protein sequence (UniProt reference sequences are facts).

rubric.evidence: Correctness verified in headless Chrome (transformers.js AutoModelForMaskedLM, WASM q8) BEFORE building: ESM-2 reconstructs the wild-type residue at hemoglobin β6 (Glu ranks #1, p≈0.30) and its per-substitution log-likelihood-ratio scores the sickle-cell mutation E6V at −2.3 (strongly deleterious) vs the conservative E6D at −1.25 — the zero-shot variant-effect signal from Meier et al. 2021. The deployed page (scripts/validate-protein-mutation-oracle.mjs) reproduces this — every prediction/score is a live forward pass, not canned.
rubric.notes: DISTINCT capability with NO built counterpart: every built fill-mask demo is a NATURAL-LANGUAGE model (English/multilingual words). This is a PROTEIN language model — a biological-sequence domain (20 amino acids) doing residue prediction + variant-effect scoring, exactly as educational-quality-scorer shared the text-classification task but was a distinct capability.

rubric.evidence: Input a protein sequence + a chosen position → the model masks that residue and returns a probability over the 20 amino acids there; the page derives, per substitution, ln P(mutant) − ln P(wild-type). This is the true masked-LM I/O read directly from logits — the sequence-likelihood variant-effect method, not an invented metric.
rubric.notes: One forward pass yields both the residue prediction and all 20 mutation scores (same masked distribution).

rubric.evidence: At-a-glance declares the model (Xenova/esm2_t12_35M_UR50D, linked, ONNX of Meta facebook/esm2_t12_35M_UR50D), the task (masked LM on protein sequences via AutoModelForMaskedLM), vocabulary (20 amino acids), training (ESM-2, ~65M UniRef sequences), quantisation (q8), backend (WASM), download (~35 MB) and license (MIT, ESM-2 upstream). The How-it-works block shows the real AutoModelForMaskedLM call and honestly explains WHY the fill-mask pipeline can't be used (the conversion omits mask_token). No invented API.
rubric.notes: License cites the clean MIT upstream (the Xenova conversion field is blank), per the OpenCV-Zoo/Basic-Pitch precedent.

rubric.evidence: Loads through the shared createModelLoader auto-init architecture (model {modelId:'Xenova/esm2_t12_35M_UR50D', runtime:'transformers.js', dtype:'q8', sizeMB:35}). First visit shows an explicit Download (~35 MB); the ONNX + tokenizer are cached by transformers.js so a returning visit auto-initialises (checking -> ready) with NO Download click. Verified: fresh profile showed Download; clicking it enabled Analyse and auto-scanned the sickle-cell position.
rubric.notes: AutoModelForMaskedLM/AutoTokenizer cache under the repo path exactly like a pipeline, so auto-init on return holds via the shared loader.

rubric.evidence: checking -> Download (~35 MB) -> ready (Analyse enabled, the pre-loaded hemoglobin auto-analysed at β6) -> per-click scanning -> prediction bars + mutation bars + readout. Scan failures surface on the page in a role=status .err region, not only the console. Verified download -> ready -> scan end-to-end and a re-scan on clicking another residue.
rubric.notes: The residue grid renders BEFORE the model finishes downloading (the sequence is local), so the page is populated immediately.

rubric.evidence: Real controls: an editable sequence textarea + Analyse button, four reference-protein sample chips (hemoglobin β / insulin / ubiquitin / lysozyme), and a clickable residue grid where each amino acid is a button that masks that position. Every control is labelled and keyboard-operable; the grid cells carry aria-labels (position + amino-acid name). No dead controls.
rubric.notes: Non-standard characters are stripped and the count is shown; the sequence is capped at 400 residues for responsiveness.

rubric.evidence: The prediction bars and the diverging mutation-effect bars are the model's real softmax + log-likelihood-ratio; the readout shows live backend + latency + the selected residue. The page is HONEST that this is a fast zero-shot SIGNAL, not a clinical verdict — the score is sequence likelihood with no knowledge of a specific structure, assay, or patient, and the 35M model is the smallest ESM-2 (larger ones are more accurate).
rubric.notes: No media: sample sequences are UniProt reference proteins (sequence data are facts, not third-party creative content), verified to behave, not asserted.

rubric.evidence: The status and scanning messages are aria-live; the residue grid is a labelled group and each cell announces its position + amino-acid name; the mutation direction is stated in text (green tolerated / red likely-damaging) and each bar carries a numeric ±LLR value, so meaning does not rely on colour alone. Focus styles on every control.
rubric.notes: The property colours on the grid are decorative; the one-letter code is the datum.

rubric.evidence: Verified with no horizontal overflow at desktop (1280px) and mobile (360px) in the end-to-end run. The residue grid wraps and scrolls vertically within a capped box; the two-column results panel collapses to one column under 560px; the readout is a flex-wrap row.
rubric.notes: Long sequences never force horizontal scroll — the grid flex-wraps.

rubric.evidence: Inference runs in a dedicated module Worker so the UI stays responsive; a single masked forward pass on the 35M model is fast on WASM, and each residue click is one pass. The ~35 MB download is one-time (cached).
rubric.notes: The small 35M ESM-2 keeps both download and latency low while still showing clear variant-effect separation.

guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: applied — scanning runs in a module Worker; the main thread only renders the residue grid and result bars.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: clicking residues stays smooth; the grid never blocks on a forward pass

guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: applied — the grid cells are aria-labelled buttons, results are aria-live, and every mutation bar shows a signed numeric LLR next to the green/red direction.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: the effect is readable as text, not just red/green

guidanceConsulted.query: masked language model output when the fill-mask pipeline is unavailable
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use the model head that matches the task; read logits directly when the high-level pipeline can't be used.

Should a larger ESM-2 (150M) be offered as an optional higher-accuracy download for variant-effect work?

summary: Protein mutation oracle (ESM-2 35M) — a distinct capability with no built counterpart: a PROTEIN language model (biological sequences, 20 amino acids), where every built fill-mask demo is natural language. Mask a residue and it predicts what belongs there and scores every substitution's log-likelihood vs wild-type — the zero-shot variant-effect method (Meier et al. 2021). Proven in the browser on transformers.js WASM q8: it reconstructs hemoglobin β6 (Glu, rank 0) and flags the sickle-cell E6V as deleterious (LLR −2.3, worse than the conservative E6D). ~35 MB, MIT (ESM-2 upstream), no media (UniProt reference sequences). A clickable residue grid + sample proteins → prediction bars + diverging mutation-effect bars + readout; index demo complete + verified. Honest that it's a fast zero-shot signal, not a clinical verdict, and the 35M model is the smallest ESM-2. A deep-mutational-scan heatmap, a variant lookup, and a larger-checkpoint toggle are recorded follow-ups. The fill-mask pipeline is unusable (conversion omits mask_token) so it runs AutoModelForMaskedLM and reads logits directly.
